phases.name: Greenfield Build
phases.tagline: Plan + 3 feature phases + P0 tests in 6 days
highlights: Jul 1 — Phase 1 core architecture: 31 files in one day (Vue 3 shell, 5 layout strategies, canvas rendering, state management)
Jul 1–2 — Phase 2 panel editing & crop; Phase 3 backgrounds, title, overlay/export
Jul 2 — 156 P0 tests implemented (Mocha/Chai unit + Playwright E2E)
Jul 3–5 — peak consumption of the project (3.5M–5.3M effective tokens/day): keyboard shortcuts end-to-end, four Phase-4 test plans, pre-Phase-4 architecture review, crop interaction bug fixes
Outcome: a fully working web app shipped to austin183.github.io in five working days

phases.name: Stabilization & Change Requests
phases.tagline: Review-fix waves, 15 change requests + 9 follow-ups, bug hunts
highlights: 4 phases of pre-commit review fixes: PNG exporter signature bug, memory/lifecycle cleanup, RAF-debounced crop preview, dedup
15 change requests (CR-01…CR-15) planned and implemented in 5 phases — multi-touch gestures, diagonal-slice angle range, background opacity, 6-handler-module refactor
9 follow-up CRs: saliency failure toast, color-swatch pivot, sidebar reorder, trackpad gestures, method extraction
Jul 7 — build-tdd agent created; Red-Green-Refactor became the standard delivery workflow

patterns: build-docs ran every day — skill refinement, code reviews, and plan authoring ran in parallel with feature work. It is the single largest consumer (13.5M effective tokens, 121 sessions); the “skill refinement” loop distilled each day’s learnings into reusable reference docs for the building-web-apps skill.

plan-bdd specs preceded nearly every multi-phase feature — title/sidebar/home, crop overlay, undo/redo expansion, mobile responsiveness, bottom sheet, and the two multi-touch fixes all started with a written BDD plan before the first TDD session.

Token intensity decayed as the codebase matured — from 5.3M effective tokens/day at the greenfield peak (Jul 5) to ~0.6–0.9M/day in the polish weeks, as change units shrank from 31-file features to targeted bug fixes.

Zero-commit days were plan/debug days — Jul 4–5, 20, 24–26, 30, and Aug 2 had no commits; their planning and diagnosis cost shows up in the next day’s commits (e.g., the Jul 19 pre-merge review directly produced the Jul 20–22 undo/redo expansion).

233 of 517 sessions have written summaries — the remainder are subagent runs (explore, world-review, diff-review) and short sessions that were not summarized. Summary coverage skews to the build-* agents, which were required to write session summaries.
